acceptance_criteria: A Twilio limiter reservation cannot remain live after its caller's send attempt times out, shuts down, or is otherwise abandoned.
Twilio pacing has a bound shorter than the owning send deadline and sheds without reserving when that bound cannot be met.
Cancellation propagates through the queue, connection bridge, adapter, limiter, and provider-call boundary.
A timed-out logical send produces at most one provider call regardless of retry count.
Queued limiter reservations are removed without breaking per-destination FIFO or rate-cap accounting.
Fake-timer integration tests prove no late provider calls after timeout, retry exhaustion, or shutdown.
blast_radius: Rate-limited Twilio agent replies and status messages, including late SMS delivery, multiplied provider calls, shutdown leakage, outbound durability ambiguity, rate-window accounting, and customer cost.
evidence_summary: Three stable live reads pinned the open identity, P4 label, update time, URL, and exact body hash while remote and API main remained de3f69bbb5648b804ea2843d310c47dda544a056. No decisive or affected path changed from that audited main. Observed exact-main agent-queue code races each send promise against a 15-second timeout but neither aborts nor awaits the losing promise before retrying. Observed Twilio sendText awaits the classic limiter acquire, whose contract never rejects and whose tests prove a 50-second wait plus serialized waiters out to 120 seconds; after reservation it calls the provider without an abort signal. Inferred from those observed seams: every timed-out attempt remains queued and can later call Twilio. The shared limiter already exposes a bounded acquire used by the Baileys governor, but Twilio keeps the unbounded method. The relevant pinned-runtime suites passed 397 of 397 tests; none integrates an agent timeout with Twilio pacing. falsifier_or_remaining_gap: The finding would be falsified if the timeout canceled the losing send promise, the limiter wait were bounded below 15 seconds, or Twilio checked caller ownership before provider handoff. Exact-main source implements none. A new cross-layer fake-timer test must measure the exact number of late provider calls.
impact: When a destination is rate-limited, the agent queue can declare multiple attempts timed out while all underlying limiter waits remain live; as slots open, those abandoned attempts can each reach Twilio and deliver duplicate SMS after the logical send was failed.
lead_verification_obligations: Re-read issue #2555 and remote main before integration.
Reconfirm the 15-second agent deadline, Twilio limiter bounds, FIFO chain, and lack of abort propagation.
Add a cross-layer RED test that advances past timeout and counts every later provider call.
Prove timeout, shutdown, and retry exhaustion cancel unowned reservations without corrupting rate accounting.
Coordinate retry disposition and idempotency semantics with issue #2553.
Run pinned agent-queue, limiter, Twilio adapter, bridge, durability, and shutdown suites on committed bytes.
